Concentration name: Digital Design and Manufacturing; Health and Built Environment; History, Theory and Society; Informal Urbanism; Sustainable Design; Urban Design
description: The Master of Advanced Architectural Design (MAAD) is a post-professional degree program for students who already hold a professional Bachelor of Architecture (BArch) or Master of Architecture (MArch) degree. The program provides the opportunity for students to pursue specialized research and design in a variety of areas. This two-semester program is intended for individuals who want to develop a specific design or research interest through further study. Successful applicants will have an interest in a particular area of architectural research or design and will have articulated a clear focus for their work. The program is specifically designed to allow students to take advantage of the faculty’s expertise in a wide range of fields.
Accreditation status: The Master of Advanced Architectural Design (MAAD) is a post-professional degree and is not accredited by the National Architectural Accrediting Board (NAAB).
Program name: Master of Advanced Architectural Design

Concentration name: Aerospace Engineering, Integrated Circuit Design
description: The Master of Advanced Study (MAS) is a professional master’s degree program for students who have already completed an undergraduate degree in engineering or a related field, and who are looking to advance their careers. These programs provide a deep technical foundation in a specific area of engineering, while also developing leadership and management skills.
Program name: Master of Advanced Study in Engineering

description: The doctoral program is designed to provide students with the research and teaching skills to examine the experiences of people of African descent and the social and cultural forces that shape those experiences. It is an interdisciplinary program that focuses on the African Diaspora in its historical and contemporary dimensions. Students are expected to master a body of knowledge in African American and African Diaspora Studies and to develop a disciplinary or multi-disciplinary concentration. The program consists of coursework, a qualifying examination, and a dissertation.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in African American Studies

description: The Department of African American Studies offers a program of graduate study leading to the MA and PhD degrees. Our graduate program is based on a multidisciplinary and interdisciplinary approach to the study of the history, culture, and society of Black people in the United States, the Caribbean, and the African diaspora. We invite applications from students who have already earned the BA or an equivalent degree. We also welcome applications from students who have already completed the MA in African American Studies or related fields for admission to the PhD program. Students should indicate on the application whether they are applying for the MA or the PhD. Students admitted for the MA may apply for the PhD program at the end of their second year. All students in the MA/PhD program are required to demonstrate competence in a language other than English.
Program name: Master of Arts in African American Studies

description: The Department of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ARE) offers a program of academic study leading to the PhD degree. The PhD program is designed to prepare students for careers in research, teaching, and government service. It provides a strong foundation in economic theory and quantitative methods and encourages students to apply these tools to problems in agricultural, environmental, and resource economics, and international development. Students are encouraged to develop their own research interests early in the program and to work closely with faculty members on research projects.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Agricultural and Resource Economics

Concentration name: Analytics
description: The Master of Analytics program at UC Berkeley is designed for individuals who want to lead the way in using data to make better decisions. The program provides students with a strong foundation in the mathematical and computational tools of analytics, as well as the practical skills needed to apply these tools to real-world problems. The program is offered by the Department of Industrial Engineering & Operations Research (IEOR) and is designed for students with a strong quantitative background who are looking to pursue careers as data scientists, analysts, or consultants in industry, government, or non-profit sectors.
Program name: Master of Analytics

description: Ancient History and Mediterranean Archaeology (AHMA) is an interdepartmental program that offers a course of study leading to the PhD degree. The group is composed of more than thirty faculty members from the following departments: Anthropology, Art History, Classics, History, Middle Eastern Languages and Cultures, and Philosophy. The program provides students with a broad background in the history and archaeology of the ancient Mediterranean and Near Eastern worlds, and offers specialized training in various disciplines and sub-fields.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Ancient History and Mediterranean Archaeology

Concentration name: Archaeology, Biological Anthropology, Sociocultural Anthropology, Medical Anthropology (joint with UCSF)
description: The Department of Anthropology offers a doctoral program in the standard subfields of the discipline—archaeology, biological anthropology, and sociocultural anthropology. In addition, there is a joint program with the University of California, San Francisco, in medical anthropology. Students in the Berkeley program have the opportunity to participate in a variety of interdisciplinary concentrations as well as in the programs of several centers and institutes.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Anthropology

description: Applied Mathematics at Berkeley has a long history. Since its beginnings, the Applied Mathematics program has focused on the creation and analysis of mathematical modeling for the physical and biological sciences and for engineering. Today the program encompasses a wide range of research in numerical analysis, scientific computing, partial differential equations, and many others. The PhD in Applied Mathematics is a program of the Department of Mathematics. Many of the requirements for the Applied Mathematics PhD program are the same as those for the Mathematics PhD program. However, the programs also have several significant differences. For example, students in Applied Mathematics must take at least two graduate courses in some field of application (such as physics, engineering, or biology).
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Applied Mathematics

Concentration name: Applied Physics, Biophysics, Chemistry and Chemical Biology, Mathematical Sciences, and Nanotechnology
description: The Applied Science & Technology (AS&T) Graduate Group offers an interdisciplinary program of study and research leading to the doctor of philosophy degree. The program is designed for students with strong backgrounds in physical science, mathematics and engineering who want to pursue research in areas that span multiple disciplines. AS&T research areas include: applied physics; biophysics; chemistry and chemical biology; mathematical sciences; and nanotechnology.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Applied Science and Technology

Concentration name: Building Science, Technology and Sustainability; History, Theory and Society; Design Theories, Methods and Practices; Architecture of Life and Living
description: The Master of Architecture program is a professional degree accredited by the National Architectural Accrediting Board (NAAB). The program is intended for students who plan to practice architecture and who have already earned a four-year non-professional bachelor's degree in architecture or a bachelor's degree in a field other than architecture. Students who have completed a professional Bachelor of Architecture degree from an NAAB-accredited (or equivalent) program are not eligible for the M.Arch degree.
Accreditation status: Accredited by the National Architectural Accrediting Board (NAAB)
Program name: Master of Architecture

Concentration name: Building Science, Technology and Sustainability; History, Theory and Society
description: The Master of Science (M.S.) in Architecture is a non-professional degree for those who wish to pursue advanced research in a specific area of architectural inquiry. This program is intended for students who already hold a professional degree in architecture (Bachelor of Architecture or Master of Architecture) or a related field, and who wish to develop a specialized focus. The M.S. degree does not lead to licensure as an architect. Research in the MS and PhD programs is generally organized into two areas of study: Building Science, Technology and Sustainability (BSTS) and History, Theory and Society (HTS).
Program name: Master of Science in Architecture

Concentration name: Building Science, Technology and Sustainability; History, Theory and Society
description: The Doctor of Philosophy in Architecture is a research-oriented degree appropriate for those who wish to pursue a career in teaching and scholarship in architecture and its related areas, or in roles in government or professional consultation which require depth in specialization and experience in research. This degree is intended to provide a student with a foundation of theoretical and methodological knowledge, and an opportunity to engage in advanced research in a specialized area of study.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Architecture

description: The MFA program in the Department of Art Practice at UC Berkeley is a two-year, small, and intensive program. Each year, roughly six to seven students are admitted into the program. MFA students are provided with individual studios at the Richmond Field Station and are expected to develop their work across multiple disciplines. Our world-renowned faculty work closely with students throughout their time in the program. The UC Berkeley MFA program culminates in a museum exhibition at the Berkeley Art Museum and Pacific Film Archive (BAMPFA). MFA students are provided with large, individual studios at the Richmond Field Station (RFS), a 15-minute shuttle ride from the main campus. These studios provide students with the space and privacy to develop their work over the course of the two-year program. This exhibition is a highlight of the program and provides students with the opportunity to show their work in a professional museum setting.
Program name: Master of Fine Arts in Art Practice

Concentration name: East Asian Studies, South Asian Studies, Southeast Asian Studies
description: The Group in Asian Studies (GAS) offers a multi-disciplinary MA program that is designed for students who want to develop a broad knowledge of Asia and who may wish to pursue a career in the private or public sector, or to prepare for further graduate study. The program provides students with the opportunity to take courses in many different departments and to work with faculty from across the university.
Program name: Master of Arts in Asian Studies

Concentration name: South Asian Studies, Southeast Asian Studies
description: The Department of South & Southeast Asian Studies offers programs of graduate study and research leading to the Master of Arts and Doctor of Philosophy degrees. The PhD program is designed to provide students with a high degree of specialized training in a particular field of South or Southeast Asian studies. Students are expected to become proficient in at least one of the major languages of the area and to acquire a thorough understanding of the history, culture, and literature of the region.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Asian Studies

description: The goal of the graduate program in astronomy is to provide students with a broad knowledge of modern observational and theoretical astrophysics, as well as an opportunity to perform research at the forefront of the field. The department's research activities include the study of the solar system, stars, and the interstellar medium; the formation and evolution of galaxies; the large-scale structure of the universe; and the big bang.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Astronomy

description: The Department of Astronomy offers a graduate program leading to the PhD degree in astrophysics. The primary objective of the graduate program is to train students for a career in research and teaching. This is accomplished through a series of core courses and an early introduction to research. Students are expected to start on a research project during their first year of study, often with one of the observational or theoretical projects currently being pursued by members of the faculty. Members of the faculty are also involved in several interdisciplinary organizations, including the Center for Particle Astrophysics, the Space Sciences Laboratory, and the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Astrophysics

description: The Department of Bioengineering at the University of California, Berkeley, and the Department of Bioengineering and Therapeutic Sciences at the University of California, San Francisco (UCSF), offer a joint graduate program in bioengineering. The program provides students with a solid foundation in the engineering and biological sciences and offers opportunities for research in a wide range of areas. The program offers a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) and a Master of Science (MS) in Bioengineering. The MS degree is typically earned by students who are already enrolled in the PhD program.
Program name: Master of Science in Bioengineering

description: The bioengineering graduate program is a joint program between the UC Berkeley and UC San Francisco (UCSF) campuses. Students in the program take classes at both campuses and may have research advisors at either campus. This unique program gives students the opportunity to learn from and conduct research with world-class faculty from two of the world’s leading universities in the fields of engineering, the biological sciences, and healthcare.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Bioengineering

description: The MA and PhD in biostatistics are offered by the Interdepartmental Group in Biostatistics. This program is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in the development and application of statistical methods in the biological and health sciences. The MA degree is designed for students who are interested in careers as biostatisticians in public health, the pharmaceutical industry, or other health-related fields. The program also provides a strong foundation for students who wish to pursue a PhD in biostatistics or a related field.
Accreditation status: The UC Berkeley School of Public Health is accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH).
Program name: Master of Arts in Biostatistics

description: The Graduate Group in Biostatistics offers programs of study leading to the MA and PhD degrees. These programs are designed to provide students with a solid foundation in the development and application of statistical and computational methods for the study of biological and health sciences. Students are trained to collaborate with researchers in a variety of fields and to contribute to the advancement of knowledge in public health and medicine.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Biostatistics

description: The Haas School of Business offers the Master of Business Administration (MBA) degree. The program is designed to provide students with a deep understanding of the fundamentals of business, while also allowing them to tailor their education to their specific interests and career goals. The curriculum is built on a foundation of 12 required courses that provide a comprehensive look at business basics. Students can then choose from a wide range of elective courses to customize their education.
Accreditation status: The Haas School of Business is accredited by AACSB International (Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business).
Program name: Master of Business Administration

Concentration name: Accounting, Business and Public Policy, Finance, Marketing, Management of Organizations (Micro and Macro), Real Estate, Operations and Information Technology Management, and Strategy
description: The Berkeley PhD Program in Business Administration offers students the opportunity to learn from and work with some of the world's leading scholars in their fields. The program's goal is to prepare students for careers in research and teaching at the world's top universities and research institutions. The PhD program is small and highly selective, with about 15-18 students entering each year. Because of the small size, students are able to work closely with faculty members in a collaborative and intellectually stimulating environment.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Business Administration

description: The Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering (CBE) offers a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Chemical Engineering and a Master of Science (MS) in Chemical Engineering. Students have the opportunity to move into new and exciting research areas in chemical engineering, including: biochemical engineering, synthetic biology and protein engineering; catalysis and reaction engineering; electrochemical engineering; polymers and soft materials; and environmental research. In addition, students can explore their interests in several cross-disciplinary programs: the Berkeley Sensors and Actuators Center, the Berkeley Stem Cell Center, the Energy Biosciences Institute, the Joint BioEnergy Institute, the Kavli Energy NanoSciences Institute, and the Synthetic Biology Engineering Research Center.
Program name: Master of Science in Chemical Engineering

description: The Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) degree in chemical engineering is primarily a research degree. The program is designed to provide students with a deep understanding of the fundamental principles of chemical engineering and to develop their ability to conduct original research. The doctoral program in chemical engineering is consistently ranked in the top few nationally by U.S. News & World Report and the National Research Council. Graduates are widely sought after for positions in academia, industry, and government laboratories.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Chemical Engineering

Concentration name: Analytical Chemistry, Chemical Biology, Inorganic Chemistry, Organic Chemistry, Physical Chemistry
description: The Department of Chemistry offers a graduate program leading to the Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) degree. The program is designed to develop the student’s ability to conduct independent research and to provide them with a strong background in the fundamentals of chemistry. The research activities in the department cover a wide variety of fields, including analytical, inorganic, organic, and physical chemistry, as well as such diverse areas as chemical biology, nuclear chemistry, and chemical physics.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Chemistry

Concentration name: Environmental Planning and Healthy Cities; Housing, Community, and Economic Development; Transportation Policy and Planning; Urban Design
description: The Master of City Planning (MCP) at UC Berkeley is a two-year professional degree accredited by the Planning Accreditation Board. The curriculum is designed to give students a strong foundation in the history and theory of planning, as well as the technical skills needed for professional practice. Students choose from one of four concentrations: Environmental Planning and Healthy Cities; Housing, Community, and Economic Development; Transportation Policy and Planning; or Urban Design.
Accreditation status: Accredited by the Planning Accreditation Board (PAB)
Program name: Master of City Planning

Concentration name: Environmental Planning and Policy; Housing, Community, and Economic Development; Land Use Planning; Transportation Policy and Planning; and Urban Design
description: The PhD in City and Regional Planning provides training for careers in research, teaching, and advanced policy analysis. Our students focus on the study of urban and regional issues in both the US and international contexts. The program is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in the theory and history of planning, as well as in the quantitative and qualitative methods used in planning research.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in City and Regional Planning

Concentration name: Energy, Civil Infrastructure and Climate; Engineering and Project Management; Environmental Engineering; GeoSystems (Geoengineering); Structural Engineering, Mechanics and Materials; Systems (Civil Systems); Transportation Engineering
description: The Civil and Environmental Engineering (CEE) Department offers a Master of Science (MS), a Master of Engineering (MEng), and a PhD. The Master of Science program emphasizes graduate-level research or specialized professional practice. The Master of Engineering (MEng) is a professional degree that provides students with a foundation in engineering and the business, management, and leadership skills to enter the workforce as an engineering leader. The PhD program is designed for students interested in research and teaching.
Program name: Master of Engineering in Civil and Environmental Engineering

Concentration name: Energy, Civil Infrastructure and Climate; Engineering and Project Management; Environmental Engineering; GeoSystems (Geoengineering); Structural Engineering, Mechanics and Materials; Systems (Civil Systems); Transportation Engineering
description: The Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering offers several degree programs for graduate students. The Master of Science (MS) and the Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) programs are designed for students who want to specialize in a particular technical area within civil and environmental engineering. The MS program usually takes two or three semesters of study. Students can also choose a professional degree program, the Master of Engineering (MEng). The Civil and Environmental Engineering department’s research and teaching are at the forefront of providing the data, models, and decision-making tools to manage the complexities of modern engineering systems.
Program name: Master of Science in Civil and Environmental Engineering

Concentration name: Energy, Civil Infrastructure and Climate; Engineering and Project Management; Environmental Engineering; GeoSystems (Geoengineering); Structural Engineering, Mechanics and Materials; Systems (Civil Systems); Transportation Engineering
description: The Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering (CEE) at UC Berkeley is a world-renowned leader in engineering education and research. We offer a wide range of graduate programs in several key areas of civil and environmental engineering. Our faculty and students work on cutting-edge research that addresses the most pressing challenges facing our society today, including climate change, urban sustainability, and resilient infrastructure. Berkeley’s CEE department is home to a vibrant and diverse community of students and faculty, and our graduates are highly sought after by employers in industry, government, and academia. Whether you’re interested in pursuing a career in research or practice, our programs will give you the skills and knowledge you need to succeed. The Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) degree is awarded as a mark of the highest achievement in preparation for a career in research and teaching. PhD students are expected to complete a series of advanced courses and to perform original and significant research leading to a dissertation.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Civil and Environmental Engineering

description: The PhD program in Classics is a five- to seven-year course of study leading to the degree of Doctor of Philosophy. The program is designed to provide students with a broad and deep knowledge of Greek and Latin language and literature, as well as the history and culture of the ancient world. Students will develop their research and teaching skills through coursework, exams, and the writing of a dissertation. The aim of the PhD program is to prepare students for careers in research and teaching at the university or college level, as well as for other professional paths that require high-level skills in analysis, communication, and research.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Classics

description: The Department of Comparative Literature at Berkeley is a community of scholars and students dedicated to the study of literature and culture across national and linguistic boundaries. Our program is built on the belief that literary study is most productive when it involves the crossover between different languages, cultures, and disciplines.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Comparative Literature

description: The Master of Science (MS) is a research-oriented degree. It is intended for students who have a master’s level of maturity in their research and wish to pursue a PhD. It can also be a terminal degree for those who wish to pursue a career in research and development in industry.
Program name: Master of Science in Computer Science

description: The PhD in Computer Science is a research-based program for students who have a prior BS or MS in a technical field (e.g., Computer Science, Math, etc.) and who wish to pursue a career in research and/or academia. The focus of the PhD program is on research. Our program is ranked as one of the top in the country and our faculty is world-renowned.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Computer Science

description: The Master of Design (MDes) at UC Berkeley is a three-semester professional graduate program that prepares students to lead the design of emerging technologies for social and technical impact. Jointly offered by the College of Engineering and the College of Environmental Design, the MDes provides an interdisciplinary curriculum that bridges technical innovation with social consciousness and creative practice. The program is designed for students who are passionate about the potential of design to address complex challenges and who want to gain the skills and knowledge to lead the design of the next generation of products, services, and environments.
Program name: Master of Design

Concentration name: AI & Data Analytics; Digital Platforms; Energy, Climate & Sustainability; Health & Medical Technologies
description: The Master of Development Engineering (MDevEng) is a professional graduate degree designed to prepare students for careers in the private and public sectors as they work to address the most pressing global challenges. Development Engineering (DevEng) is an emerging field that integrates engineering, social sciences, and design to address development challenges through the lens of human-centered design and social impact. The program provides students with a multidisciplinary education, emphasizing the development, implementation, and scaling of technological solutions in low-resource settings. Students will learn to analyze complex problems, design sustainable and impactful interventions, and evaluate their effectiveness. The three-semester curriculum includes core coursework in development engineering, specialized tracks, and a capstone project.
Program name: Master of Development Engineering

description: The Master of Development Practice (MDP) at UC Berkeley is a cross-disciplinary professional degree program that prepares students to address the world’s most pressing challenges. Drawing on the expertise of the Goldman School of Public Policy and faculty from across campus, the MDP provides students with the skills and knowledge needed to become leaders in sustainable development. The program combines rigorous academic training with practical, hands-on experience through a summer internship and a capstone project. Students learn to integrate insights from across the natural sciences, social sciences, and management to develop innovative solutions to complex problems.
Program name: Master of Development Practice

description: Earth and Planetary Science (EPS) is a multidisciplinary field of study that focuses on the physics, chemistry, and biology of the Earth and other planets. EPS research at Berkeley involves faculty and students in the fields of atmospheric science, biogeochemistry, climate science, ecology, geochemistry, geodesy, geology, geomorphology, geophysics, glaciology, mineralogy, paleontology, planetary science, and seismology. EPS students and faculty use a wide range of tools, including laboratory experiments, field observations, remote sensing, and numerical modeling. Our department is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive environment where all students can thrive.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Earth and Planetary Science

Concentration name: Chinese, Japanese, or Buddhist Studies
description: The Department of East Asian Languages and Cultures (EALC) offers a program of graduate study leading to the Doctor of Philosophy (PhD). The primary goal of the PhD program is to prepare students for a career in research and teaching at the university level. Students specialize in one of three areas: Chinese, Japanese, or Buddhist Studies. The department also participates in several interdisciplinary doctoral programs, including the Designated Emphasis (DE) in Film Studies, Renaissance and Early Modern Studies, Folklore, and Women, Gender, and Sexuality.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in East Asian Languages and Cultures

Concentration name: Behavioral Economics, Development Economics, Econometrics, Economic History, Economic Theory, Industrial Organization, International Economics, Labor Economics, Macroeconomics, Public Economics
description: The PhD program at Berkeley is designed for students interested in pursuing advanced study and conducting original research in Economics. The primary objective of the graduate program is to educate students for careers in research and teaching. The program is designed to provide students with the tools and techniques of modern economic analysis, as well as to encourage them to develop their own research interests. The PhD program is a full-time, in-residence program, and is completed, on average, in 5 to 6 years. Students take core courses in their first year and then specialize in two fields of their choice during their second and third years. The remainder of the program is spent conducting original research and writing a dissertation.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Economics

Concentration name: Critical Studies of Race, Class, and Gender; Cultural Studies of Sport in Education; Language, Literacy, and Culture; Learning Sciences and Human Development; Policy, Politics, and Leadership; Quantitative Methods and Evaluation; Social Research Methodologies
description: The Berkeley School of Education offers a Master of Arts in Education for students who wish to pursue a research-focused degree. This program is designed for students who are interested in pursuing a doctoral degree in the future or who are seeking a career in educational research, policy, or practice. The MA degree is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in educational theory, research methods, and a specialized area of study. The MA degree requires students to complete a minimum of 24 units of coursework and a capstone project (either a thesis or a comprehensive examination).
Program name: Master of Arts in Education

Concentration name: Critical Studies of Race, Class, and Gender; Cultural Studies of Sport in Education; Development in Language, Literacy and Culture; Learning Sciences and Human Development; Policy, Politics, and Leadership; Quantitative Methods and Evaluation; Social and Cultural Studies; Special Education (joint program with SF State)
description: The Graduate School of Education offers a PhD and MA/PhD in Education with several areas of study. The doctoral program is designed to produce scholars who will conduct research and teach in universities and other research settings. The Master’s/Doctoral program is for students who do not already have a Master’s degree. Students are admitted to one of the following areas of study: Critical Studies of Race, Class, and Gender; Cultural Studies of Sport in Education; Development in Language, Literacy and Culture; Learning Sciences and Human Development; Policy, Politics, and Leadership; Quantitative Methods and Evaluation; Social and Cultural Studies; and Special Education (joint program with SF State).
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Education

Concentration name: Leaders for Equity and Democracy
description: The LEAD EdD program is designed for working educational leaders who are committed to disrupting systems of privilege and power to achieve more equitable outcomes for students. The program is a three-year, cohort-based, executive-style program that integrates theory, research, and practice to prepare leaders to transform educational organizations.
Program name: Doctor of Education in Education

Concentration name: ['Data Science and Systems', 'Physical Electronics and Integrated Circuits', 'Robotics and Embedded Software', 'Signal Processing and Communications', 'Visual Computing and Computer Graphics']
description: The Master of Engineering (M.Eng.) in Electrical Engineering & Computer Sciences is a professional program designed for students who plan to pursue a career in industry. The program's core curriculum consists of a capstone project and courses in leadership and technology management, which are supplemented by technical electives in the student's chosen area of concentration.
Program name: Master of Engineering in Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences

description: The Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences (EECS) offers two graduate programs in Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences: the Master of Integrated Circuits (offered only through the Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences) and the Master of Science (MS) and Doctor of Philosophy (PhD). The Master of Science (MS) is a research-oriented degree that can be earned as a terminal degree or as the first step toward the PhD. This program is available only to students who are currently enrolled in a PhD program at UC Berkeley or who have been admitted to a PhD program at UC Berkeley. The PhD is a research-oriented degree intended for students who wish to pursue a career in research and teaching. The Master of Engineering (MEng) is a professional degree designed for students who want to enter the industry with a high level of technical expertise and a grounding in business and management.
Program name: Master of Science in Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences

Concentration name: Computer Science, Electrical Engineering
description: The Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences (EECS) offers two graduate programs in Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences: the Master of Science (MS) and the Doctor of Philosophy (PhD). The Master of Science (MS) is a research-oriented degree that can be earned in two semesters (Plan II, which requires a project) or three semesters (Plan I, which requires a thesis). The Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) is intended for students who desire a career in research. The program requires a minimum of two years of study, a qualifying examination, and a dissertation. Research in the department is organized into several areas: Artificial Intelligence (AI), Biosystems & Computational Biology (BIO), Communications & Networking (COMNET), Computer Architecture & Engineering (ARC), Control, Intelligent Systems, and Robotics (CIR), Database Management Systems (DBMS), Design of Electronic Systems (DES), Education (EDUC), Energy (ENE), Graphics (GR), Human-Computer Interaction (HCI), Integrated Circuits (INC), Micro/Nano Electro Mechanical Systems (MEMS), Operating Systems & Networking (OSNT), Programming Systems (PS), Scientific Computing (SCI), Security (SEC), Signal Processing (SP), Theory (THY).
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences

description: The Energy and Resources Group (ERG) is an interdisciplinary academic graduate unit at the University of California, Berkeley. ERG’s mission is to provide education and research for a sustainable environment and a just society. To this end, ERG provides the tools to help students and researchers develop the skills to bridge disciplines and the knowledge to work across the boundaries of traditional departments. ERG students are challenged to integrate the methods of the natural and social sciences into an approach that addresses the complex challenges facing the world. ERG focuses on issues such as global climate change, sustainable development, resource governance, renewable energy, and environmental justice. ERG graduates go on to work in academia, government, non-profit organizations, and the private sector.
Program name: Master of Arts in Energy and Resources

description: The Energy and Resources Group (ERG) is a unique, interdisciplinary graduate program at the University of California, Berkeley. ERG provides an environment for research and teaching on the complex challenges facing our environment, our societies, and our energy and resource systems. The ERG Master’s program is a two-year program designed to provide students with a broad, interdisciplinary education in energy and resources. The program leads to either a Master of Arts (MA) or a Master of Science (MS) degree. The curriculum is intended to help students develop the analytical tools and the conceptual framework to address the complex issues of resource management, environmental impact, and sustainable development.
Program name: Master of Science in Energy and Resources

description: The Energy and Resources Group (ERG) is an interdisciplinary academic unit of the University of California, Berkeley. ERG’s mission is to provide education and research for a sustainable environment and a just society. To this end, ERG offers two professional master’s degrees (MA and MS) and a doctoral degree (PhD). The ERG curriculum is designed to provide students with a broad understanding of the technical, economic, social, and political aspects of energy and resource issues, as well as the tools to analyze and solve problems in these areas. ERG students and faculty come from a wide range of backgrounds, including the natural sciences, engineering, social sciences, and humanities.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Energy and Resources

description: Our PhD program provides students with a broad and deep foundation in English and American literature, as well as the specialized skills needed to carry out original research in a chosen area of study. Students work closely with faculty members who are leaders in their fields, and they benefit from the resources of a world-class research university. The program is designed to be completed in six years, and it includes coursework, a qualifying examination, and a dissertation. Graduate students in English at Berkeley are part of a vibrant intellectual community that includes over 100 PhD students and 50 faculty members.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in English

Concentration name: Global Health & Environment, Industrial Hygiene, Occupational and Environmental Health Nursing
description: The Master of Science (MS) in Environmental Health Sciences provides students with a strong foundation in the principles and practices of environmental health. This degree program is designed for students with a background in the basic sciences who wish to pursue careers in research or professional practice. Students in the MS program will gain expertise in identifying and assessing environmental and occupational hazards, understanding the health effects of these hazards, and developing strategies to prevent or control exposure. The MS program typically takes two years to complete and requires a combination of coursework and research. Students will work closely with faculty mentors to develop a research project and complete a thesis.
Accreditation status: The UC Berkeley School of Public Health is accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH).
Program name: Master of Science in Environmental Health Sciences

description: The Environmental Health Sciences (EHS) program at UC Berkeley is concerned with the effects of environmental and occupational exposures on human health and with the assessment and control of these exposures. The Doctor of Philosophy degree (PhD) in Environmental Health Sciences is an academic research degree that is intended for students who have an interest in academic or research careers. The Division of Environmental Health Sciences (EHS) provides students with the skills required for research and practice in the prevention of injuries and illnesses caused by various exposures in the workplace and the environment. Students specialize in one of several areas within environmental health, though the integrated nature of the program ensures that all students obtain a thorough understanding of the field as a whole. Core areas of focus include: climate change and health; environmental and occupational epidemiology; and toxicology, environmental chemistry, and exposure assessment.
Accreditation status: The School of Public Health is fully accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH).
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Environmental Health Sciences

Concentration name: Ecosystem Sciences, Organisms & Environment, and Society & Environment
description: The ESPM PhD program is one of the premier environmental research and education programs in the world. Our mission is to educate the next generation of scholars and leaders who will address the most pressing environmental challenges of our time. ESPM provides a diverse and interdisciplinary environment for graduate study, where students work across natural and social science disciplines to understand and manage the earth's environment.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Environmental Science, Policy, and Management

description: The MS in Epidemiology provides students with a strong foundation in epidemiologic and biostatistical methods and their application to a wide range of public health problems. The program is designed for students who want to pursue a career in epidemiologic research or who intend to pursue a doctoral degree. Through a combination of coursework and a master’s thesis, students will learn to design, conduct, and analyze epidemiologic studies and to communicate their findings to scientific and professional audiences.
Accreditation status: The UC Berkeley School of Public Health is fully accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH).
Program name: Master of Science in Epidemiology

description: Epidemiology is a department-wide program at the UC Berkeley School of Public Health. Our epidemiology graduate programs offer students a choice of three degrees: Master of Public Health (MPH), Master of Science (MS), and Doctor of Philosophy (PhD). Students in our program gain the skills to become highly-trained, independent researchers who can apply epidemiological methods to various public health issues. Our students work closely with faculty members in a variety of areas of public health, including infectious diseases, chronic diseases, maternal and child health, environmental health, and social epidemiology. Our students also have the opportunity to collaborate with faculty members in other departments at UC Berkeley and at other institutions. The PhD in epidemiology provides students with the skills to become independent researchers who can apply epidemiological methods to a wide range of public health issues, preparing them for careers in academia, research institutions, and government agencies.
Accreditation status: The UC Berkeley School of Public Health is fully accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH).
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Epidemiology

description: The Department of Ethnic Studies at the University of California, Berkeley, offers a PhD in Ethnic Studies. The program is internationally recognized for its leadership in the development of comparative ethnic studies. The PhD program provides an interdisciplinary and comparative framework for studying the historical, social, and cultural productions of power and social difference. The curriculum focuses on the histories, cultures, and politics of racial and ethnic groups in the United States and globally, with particular emphasis on African American, Asian American/Pacific Islander, Chicana/o/Latina/o, and Native American/Indigenous peoples.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Ethnic Studies

description: The graduate program in Film & Media at UC Berkeley is designed for students who want to develop a deep understanding of film and media history, theory, and criticism. The program emphasizes the interdisciplinary nature of film and media studies, and students are encouraged to draw on the resources of the entire university. Film & Media at Berkeley is a leading center for the study of cinema and new media, with a world-renowned faculty and a vibrant graduate student community.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Film and Media

description: The Berkeley Master of Financial Engineering program prepares you for a career in finance by combining advanced training in financial theory with the practical skills needed for the quantitative finance industry. Our curriculum is designed to provide you with a deep understanding of finance, economics, mathematics, and computer science. Since its inception in 2000, the Berkeley MFE has been a leader in the field, consistently ranking among the top programs in the world, providing students with the knowledge and skills they need to succeed in the fast-paced world of quantitative finance.
Program name: Master of Financial Engineering

description: The Folklore Graduate Program offers an M.A. degree. Folklore at Berkeley is interdisciplinary and students have the opportunity to design an individual program of study with the help of a faculty advisor. The Berkeley faculty includes many distinguished scholars from across the campus with a specific interest in folklore. Folklore is a multifaceted discipline that draws from many other fields, including anthropology, linguistics, literature, history, sociology, and psychology. Students interested in pursuing a graduate degree in folklore should have a strong background in one or more of these areas.
Program name: Master of Arts in Folklore

description: The Department of French offers a Ph.D. in French. It does not offer a terminal Master’s degree. All students are admitted to the Ph.D. program, but have the option of receiving an M.A. en route to the Ph.D. Once admitted, students follow a program of study consisting of course work, a qualifying examination, and a dissertation. Students are expected to become proficient in the standard areas of French and Francophone literature and culture, while also pursuing their own particular research interests. They are also expected to develop a high level of proficiency in the French language. The department provides a rigorous training in the teaching of French at all levels, and students are given the opportunity to teach both language and literature courses.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in French

description: The graduate program is primarily a PhD program, although students may receive an MA degree in the course of their doctoral studies. (The department does not offer a terminal MA degree.) The Berkeley Geography graduate program is one of the most highly ranked in the country. Our faculty and students have a wide range of interests, and the program is designed to be flexible to allow students to pursue their own research agendas. Geography at Berkeley is a small, highly-ranked department that offers students a chance to work with a distinguished faculty. Our graduate students are a talented and diverse group, and they go on to careers in academia, government, and the private sector. Themes of the department include: Development & Political Ecology, Global Change and Ecosystems, Global Environmental Processes, Geomorphology, Urban Studies, Place, Race and Power, and GIS and Remote Sensing.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Geography

Concentration name: German Literature and Culture, Germanic Linguistics
description: The Department of German at the University of California, Berkeley offers a program of graduate study leading to the Ph.D. Students may specialize in either German Literature and Culture or Germanic Linguistics. The program is designed to provide students with a comprehensive knowledge of the German language, its history, and its literature and culture from the earliest times to the present, while at the same time encouraging them to develop their own research interests within a broad range of theoretical and interdisciplinary perspectives. Students are prepared for careers in research and teaching at the college and university level.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in German

Concentration name: Global Development, Global Societies and Cultures, Global Governance
description: The Master of Arts (MA) in Global Studies is a one-year, interdisciplinary program designed for students who want to develop a deeper understanding of the global processes that shape our world. The program is ideal for students who are looking for a rigorous academic experience that will prepare them for a variety of careers in the public, private, and non-profit sectors, or for further graduate study.
Program name: Master of Arts in Global Studies

Concentration name: health economics, health services and policy research, and organizational behavior
description: The Doctoral Program in Health Policy at the University of California, Berkeley, provides students with the breadth and depth of knowledge and the specialized skills to perform high-quality, innovative research in health policy and health services. This multidisciplinary program, which leads to a PhD degree, is designed for students interested in pursuing careers in teaching and research in academic institutions, and in research and policy analysis in government and in the private sector.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Health Policy

description: The Department of Spanish & Portuguese offers programs of study leading to the PhD in Hispanic Languages and Literatures. The program provides students with a high degree of professional preparation for a career in university teaching and research. It is designed to ensure that students have a broad knowledge of the literature and culture of the Hispanic and Lusophone worlds, as well as the critical and linguistic tools necessary for specialized research.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Hispanic Languages and Literatures

description: The Department of History offers a program of graduate study leading to the Ph.D. in History. The program is designed to provide students with the opportunity for advanced study in history, to train them in the methods of historical research, and to prepare them for careers in teaching and research. The department offers training in a wide range of geographical and thematic fields, from ancient history to the present day, and is committed to preparing its students for professional success both within and outside of academia.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in History

Concentration name: Critical Theory, Film Studies, Gender, Women and Sexuality, Medieval Studies, New Media, Renaissance and Early Modern Studies, Science and Technology Studies
description: The Graduate Program in History of Art is designed to prepare students for careers in college and university teaching, museum work, and other positions of intellectual leadership in the visual arts. The program is specifically directed toward the PhD. We do not offer a separate Master’s degree, although students may earn an MA on the way to the PhD. The Department of History of Art at Berkeley provides its graduate students with diverse opportunities for intellectual growth, professional training, and financial support. These range from departmental and campus resources to external fellowships and internships.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in History of Art

Concentration name: Data Science and Systems Engineering, Financial Technology, Intellectual Property and Strategy, and Management Science and Engineering
description: The Master of Engineering (M.Eng.) program is a professional program that combines advanced technical courses with leadership and management courses. The Berkeley Master of Engineering (M.Eng.) in Industrial Engineering & Operations Research is a full-time, one-year professional program that blends rigorous technical training with leadership and management coursework. It is designed for students who want to become engineering leaders in their field. The program allows students to customize their experience by choosing from a range of concentrations and electives, and provides opportunities to work on real-world projects with industry partners.
Program name: Master of Engineering in Industrial Engineering and Operations Research

description: The Department of Industrial Engineering and Operations Research at UC Berkeley offers three graduate programs: the Doctor of Philosophy (PhD), the Master of Science (MS), and the Master of Engineering (MEng). Our programs are consistently ranked among the top in the nation by U.S. News & World Report. Students come from all over the world to work with our award-winning faculty in one of the most exciting and productive departments in the country.
Program name: Master of Science in Industrial Engineering and Operations Research

description: The IEOR Department offers a Ph.D. in IEOR, where students participate in an advanced, research-oriented program of study. Students focus on a specific research area of their choice. UC Berkeley’s graduate programs are consistently ranked among the top in the nation. The goal of the Ph.D. program is to prepare students for careers in research and teaching at the university level, or for research and development positions in industry or government.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Industrial Engineering and Operations Research

description: The Master of Information and Cybersecurity (MICS) is a multi-disciplinary professional degree program. Delivered online, MICS provides students with the proficiency in the technologies and practices of systems, software, and network security, as well as an understanding of the legal, policy, and ethical issues surrounding cybersecurity. Students will learn to develop and manage secure systems, analyze and respond to security threats, and understand the broader social and political implications of cybersecurity. The program is designed for working professionals with a background in computer science, information technology, or a related field.
Accreditation status: The University of California, Berkeley is accredited by the Western Association of Schools and Colleges (WASC).
Program name: Master of Information and Cybersecurity

description: The Master of Information and Data Science (MIDS) is a professional degree program designed to train data science leaders. Delivered online, the MIDS program features a multidisciplinary curriculum that includes computer science, statistics, social science, management, and law. Students learn to derive insights from complex and unstructured data, using the latest tools and analytical methods. Students explore the entire data science lifecycle, from data collection and processing to analysis and communication.
Program name: Master of Information and Data Science

description: The Master of Information Management and Systems (MIMS) program is a 48-unit, two-year professional degree program designed to train students for careers as information professionals. To prepare students for such careers, the MIMS program provides a solid foundation in the concepts and techniques of information management, as well as the ability to apply those concepts and techniques in a variety of settings. The program is interdisciplinary, drawing on faculty and courses from across the Berkeley campus, including computer science, law, business, and the social sciences.
Program name: Master of Information Management and Systems

description: The Ph.D. in Information Management and Systems is a research-oriented degree program for students who wish to prepare for careers in research and teaching at the university level or for research and leadership positions in industry or government. The program is designed for students with diverse backgrounds — including the social sciences, humanities, and computer and physical sciences — who have a common interest in the study of information. PhD students work with faculty on original research and will develop a deep understanding of the social, technical, and policy issues that surround information.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Information Management and Systems

description: Graduate study in the Department of Integrative Biology (IB) at the University of California, Berkeley, offers a program of study and research leading to the Doctor of Philosophy degree. The Department of Integrative Biology is one of the largest departments on the UC Berkeley campus. It focuses on the integration of structure and function in the evolution and ecology of organisms. Research in the department spans all levels of biological organization, from the molecular and organismal to the community and ecosystem levels. The department includes over 45 faculty members, over 100 graduate students, and approximately 100 postdoctoral fellows and visiting scholars. Areas of expertise include ecology, evolutionary biology, paleontology, physiology, functional morphology, biomechanics, and human biology.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Integrative Biology

description: The Department of Italian Studies offers a program of study leading to the PhD in Italian Studies. The program is designed to provide students with a broad and rigorous training in Italian literature and culture from the medieval period to the present. The department’s faculty are specialists in a wide range of areas, including medieval and Renaissance studies, 18th- to 20th-century literature, film studies, and cultural studies.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Italian Studies

description: Our two-year Master of Journalism program is widely considered to be one of the best in the country. Our unique curriculum allows students to gain a foundation in the basics of reporting, writing and editing, while developing professional-level skills in multiple platforms: audio, documentary, multimedia, narrative writing, photography, and video journalism. Throughout the program, students can choose to work in any of these media or a combination of several, focusing on everything from investigative reporting to local news. This multiplatform approach gives our graduates an advantage in an increasingly digital and diverse professional world. It prepares them to be leaders in the field and provides them with the flexibility to thrive in any newsroom. Students in the MJ program spend two full years on campus. The first year is focused on learning foundational skills and creating high-quality work in specific media platforms. The second year is devoted to deep, original reporting on a master’s project or a documentary film. MJ students can also apply for a concurrent degree in another field. We currently offer three concurrent degrees: Journalism and Law (JD/MJ), Journalism and Asian Studies (MA/MJ), and Journalism and Public Health (MPH/MJ).
Accreditation status: The UC Berkeley Graduate School of Journalism is accredited by the Accrediting Council on Education in Journalism and Mass Communications (ACEJMC).
Program name: Master of Journalism

description: The Jurisprudence and Social Policy (JSP) Program is a unique PhD program that provides interdisciplinary study in law and legal institutions. At the Jurisprudence and Social Policy Program (JSP), we study law using the concepts and methods of the humanities and social sciences. As the first program of its kind in the United States, JSP has a long-standing commitment to cross-disciplinary scholarship. JSP is located in the Law School, but our faculty and students come from many disciplines, including history, political science, sociology, economics, philosophy and psychology. We emphasize the integration of law and legal institutions with the theories and methods of the social sciences and humanities. While some of our students pursue a JD alongside their PhD, JSP is a research-intensive program that does not require a law degree. Our mission is to produce scholars and leaders who can apply rigorous interdisciplinary research to the most pressing legal and social issues of our time.
Program name: Master of Arts in Jurisprudence and Social Policy

Concentration name: Economics, History, Philosophy, Political Science, and Sociology
description: Jurisprudence and Social Policy (JSP) is a unique interdisciplinary graduate program at Berkeley Law. JSP was the first of its kind in the United States, offering a Ph.D. degree for the study of law from the perspective of various social science and humanities disciplines: economics, history, philosophy, political science, and sociology. The JSP program provides a setting for students to analyze legal ideas, institutions, and processes from an empirical and normative perspective. Students in the program develop the necessary expertise to become scholars in their chosen fields of study and to teach in law schools and departments of social science and humanities.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Jurisprudence and Social Policy

description: The Master of Landscape Architecture (M.L.A.) degree is a professional degree, which is accredited by the Landscape Architectural Accreditation Board (LAAB). The program offers two tracks of study: a three-year program (M.L.A. I) for students who have an undergraduate degree in a field other than landscape architecture or architecture; and a two-year program (M.L.A. II) for students who have a prior professional degree in landscape architecture or architecture. The M.L.A. program prepares students for leadership in the profession of landscape architecture. It is an intensive course of study that provides students with the necessary skills to design at a variety of scales—from the site to the region—and to engage with the complex social, environmental, and aesthetic issues facing the built environment today. The program’s curriculum is grounded in a strong foundation of design, ecology, and technology, and it emphasizes the importance of research and critical thinking in the design process. The M.L.A. program in the Department of Landscape Architecture and Environmental Planning (LAEP) at the Berkeley campus is one of the oldest and most prestigious landscape architecture programs in the United States.
Accreditation status: Accredited by the Landscape Architectural Accreditation Board (LAAB)
Program name: Master of Landscape Architecture

description: The PhD program in Landscape Architecture and Environmental Planning (LAEP) is a research-oriented degree that emphasizes the development of specialized knowledge in various facets of the field. Students pursue individual research interests under the guidance of faculty experts, contributing to the academic and professional knowledge base of landscape architecture and environmental planning. Areas of research may include environmental history, social and cultural aspects of design, ecological design and planning, and urban design.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Landscape Architecture and Environmental Planning

description: The Master of Arts (MA) in Latin is a terminal degree program designed to provide students with a broad and deep knowledge of Latin literature and language. The program is particularly suited for those who wish to teach Latin at the secondary school level or who wish to prepare for further graduate study in classics or related fields.
Program name: Master of Arts in Latin

description: The Doctor of Philosophy in Latin American Studies is a research-oriented program designed for students who wish to focus on a particular problem or theme related to Latin America while also gaining expertise in two different disciplines. Students work with a faculty committee that reflects their multidisciplinary interests. The program is intended to produce scholars who are well-grounded in a particular discipline, but who can also think and work across disciplinary boundaries. Each student’s program is unique, organized around a particular problem or theme and two disciplines.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Latin American Studies

Concentration name: Environmental Law
description: The Berkeley Law LL.M. Certificate in Environmental Law recognizes that students have successfully completed a course of study and have specialized in environmental and energy law. To earn the certificate, students must complete at least 12 units of coursework from the list below, including a 1-unit ‘foundational’ course (Environmental Law and Policy for LLMs) and a 1-unit ‘capstone’ experience (the LLM Environmental and Energy Law Research Seminar or a faculty-approved research paper).
Program name: Master of Laws

description: The Doctor of Juridical Science (J.S.D.) is Berkeley Law’s most advanced law degree. It is designed for those who want to pursue a career in legal education and who want to engage in scholarly research and writing in a particular field of law. J.S.D. candidates are expected to produce a dissertation that will make a substantial and original contribution to legal scholarship.
Program name: Doctor of Juridical Science

Concentration name: Business Law, Energy & Clean Technology Law, Environmental Law, Intellectual Property & Technology Law, International Law, and Public Interest & Social Justice Law
description: Berkeley Law is one of the nation’s premier law schools. Its curriculum is one of the most comprehensive and innovative in the country, and its faculty is composed of many of the world’s leading scholars and practitioners. The law school offers several degree programs, including the Juris Doctor (J.D.), the Master of Laws (LL.M.), the Doctor of the Science of Law (J.S.D.), and the Ph.D. in Jurisprudence and Social Policy (JSP). The law school also offers several joint degree programs with other departments on campus. Berkeley Law students are high achievers with a commitment to making a difference. They are also incredibly diverse in terms of their backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives.
Accreditation status: The School of Law is accredited by the Council of the Section of Legal Education and Admissions to the Bar of the American Bar Association.
Program name: Juris Doctor

description: The Department of Linguistics offers a graduate program leading to the Doctor of Philosophy degree. The program is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in the core areas of linguistics and to allow them to specialize in one or more areas of research. The department has a long-standing reputation for excellence in research and teaching, and our faculty and students are engaged in a wide range of linguistic research, including phonetics, phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics, pragmatics, historical linguistics, sociolinguistics, psycholinguistics, and cognitive linguistics.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Linguistics

description: The Group in Logic and the Methodology of Science at the University of California, Berkeley, offers an interdisciplinary program of study leading to the degree of Doctor of Philosophy. The program is designed for students with a strong background in mathematics or philosophy who wish to pursue research in logic, the foundations of mathematics, or the philosophy of science.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Logic and the Methodology of Science

Concentration name: Biomaterials, Chemical and Electrochemical Materials, Computational Materials, Electronic, Magnetic and Optical Materials, and Structural Materials
description: The Department of Materials Science and Engineering (MSE) offers graduate programs leading to the Master of Engineering (MEng), Master of Science (MS), and the Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) degrees. Materials science and engineering is a multidisciplinary field that applies the fundamental principles of physics, chemistry, and biology to design, characterize, and manufacture the materials that underpin our modern world. Graduate students in MSE have the opportunity to work with world-class faculty on cutting-edge research in areas such as biomaterials, chemical and electrochemical materials, computational materials, electronic, magnetic and optical materials, and structural materials. The Master of Engineering (MEng) is a professionally oriented program designed to develop business and leadership skills for students who want to become leaders in the technology industry.
Program name: Master of Engineering in Materials Science and Engineering

Concentration name: Biomaterials; Chemical and Electrochemical Materials Science and Engineering; Computational Materials Science and Engineering; Electronic, Magnetic and Optical Materials; Structural Materials
description: Materials Science and Engineering (MSE) is a multidisciplinary field that explores the relationship between the structure of materials at atomic or molecular scales and their macroscopic properties. Materials scientists and engineers work to understand and manipulate these relationships to design and develop new materials for a wide range of applications, including electronics, energy, medicine, and aerospace.
Program name: Master of Science in Materials Science and Engineering

description: Materials Science and Engineering (MSE) is a discipline that investigates the relationship between the structure of materials at atomic or molecular scales and their macroscopic properties. Materials scientists and engineers at Berkeley and elsewhere are at the forefront of modern technology. Many of the most exciting areas of engineering involve the design and development of new materials for applications in the electronics, computing, energy, and healthcare industries. MSE is a highly interdisciplinary field, drawing upon the principles of physics, chemistry, and biology to understand and control the behavior of materials. Graduate students at Berkeley work with faculty and researchers across various departments and laboratories, including the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory. Students in the graduate program learn the basic principles of materials science and engineering through a core curriculum and specialized courses in their research areas. They also gain research experience by working with world-class faculty in state-of-the-art facilities. The program provides students with the skills and knowledge needed to pursue careers in academia, industry, or government.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Materials Science and Engineering

description: The Ph.D. program is designed for students who wish to pursue a career in research and/or teaching. The centerpiece of the program is the doctoral dissertation, which must be a finished piece of original research. There are no course requirements; however, students are expected to complete two semesters of a proseminar and three semesters as a Graduate Student Instructor (GSI). The Ph.D. is awarded on the basis of a demonstration of significant achievement in math research and a high level of proficiency in the field. Specializations within the Department of Mathematics include almost all the major areas of contemporary research: algebra, analysis, geometry, topology, logic, number theory, and many others. We also offer an emphasis in applied mathematics.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Mathematics

Concentration name: Advanced Energy Technology, Aerospace Engineering, Biomechanics, Control of Robotic and Autonomous Systems, Design, Fluids and Ocean, MEMS/Nano, Mechanics, Modeling and Simulation of Physical Systems, Product Design
description: The Master of Engineering (M.Eng.) program is a professional degree designed for students who plan to enter industry and want to develop their technical skills and leadership potential. The program combines advanced technical coursework with a core leadership curriculum in business and management. Students choose from one of 10 concentrations and complete a capstone project that focuses on solving real-world challenges.
Program name: Master of Engineering in Mechanical Engineering

Concentration name: Biomechanical Engineering, Controls, Design, Dynamics, Energy Science and Technology, Fluid Mechanics, Manufacturing, Materials and Mechanics, Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems (MEMS), Nanoscale Science and Engineering, Ocean Engineering
description: The Mechanical Engineering Department at Berkeley offers four graduate degrees: the Master of Engineering (M.Eng.), the Master of Science (M.S.), the Master of Science/Doctor of Philosophy (M.S./Ph.D.), and the Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.). In the Mechanical Engineering department, we have a very clear mission: to provide our students with the best possible education, to conduct research that will benefit society, and to serve our profession and the community. Our graduate program is one of the best in the world, and our students have the opportunity to work with world-class faculty on cutting-edge research.
Program name: Master of Science in Mechanical Engineering

Concentration name: Biomechanical Engineering, Controls, Design, Dynamics, Energy Science and Technology, Fluids, Manufacturing, Materials, Mechanics, Micro and Nano Systems, and Ocean Engineering
description: The Ph.D. degree is intended for students who wish to pursue a career in research and/or teaching in an academic or industrial environment. It is awarded for original and significant research as well as for proficiency in the chosen area of study. This research is expected to be of such high quality that it could be published in a peer-reviewed journal.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Mechanical Engineering
Master of Arts in Media Studies

description: The Joint Degree Program in Medical Anthropology is a Ph.D. program offered by the Department of Anthropology at UC Berkeley and the Department of Humanities and Social Sciences (formerly Anthropology, History and Social Medicine) at UCSF. The program is designed to provide students with a comprehensive background in social and cultural anthropology, and to prepare them for research and teaching in the field of medical anthropology.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Medical Anthropology

description: The Metabolic Biology graduate program focuses on the study of the biochemical and molecular basis of metabolic processes and how these are integrated at the level of the whole organism. Our faculty research a broad range of topics, including the control of metabolism and the physiological consequences of metabolic dysregulation, such as obesity, diabetes, and cancer. Students in the program gain expertise in metabolic regulation, nutrition, and disease pathophysiology. The program offers both a Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) and a Master of Science (M.S.) degree.
Program name: Master of Science in Metabolic Biology

description: The graduate program in Metabolic Biology (MB) offers a program of study and research leading to the PhD or MS degree. The MB program focuses on the study of how nutrients and metabolites regulate gene expression, signal transduction, and physiological processes. Research in the MB program spans a wide range of topics, including the regulation of lipid, carbohydrate, and protein metabolism; the molecular basis of metabolic diseases such as obesity, diabetes, and cardiovascular disease; and the role of metabolism in aging and cancer. Students in the MB program will receive training in the latest techniques in biochemistry, molecular biology, cell biology, and physiology, and will have the opportunity to work with world-renowned faculty in a highly collaborative and interdisciplinary research environment. The goal of the program is to prepare students for careers in academia, industry, and government, where they can make significant contributions to the field of metabolic biology and the improvement of human health.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Metabolic Biology

description: The Graduate Program in Microbiology is a PhD program that involves 50+ faculty from diverse departments, including Plant & Microbial Biology; Molecular & Cell Biology; Public Health; Chemistry; Civil & Environmental Engineering; Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering; and Environmental Science, Policy & Management. Research is focused in four areas: Ecology and Evolution; Genetics and Development; Physiology and Biochemistry; and Host-Microbe Interactions.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Microbiology

description: The Middle Eastern Studies program is designed for students who wish to pursue a multidisciplinary program of study and research on the Middle East. The program is intended to allow students to combine a social science or humanities discipline with the study of a particular region or period of the Middle East. Students are expected to attain a high level of proficiency in at least one Middle Eastern language.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Middle Eastern Studies

Concentration name: Biochemistry, Biophysics and Structural Biology; Cell Biology, Development and Physiology; Genetics, Genomics, Evolution, and Development; Immunology and Molecular Medicine; Neurobiology
description: The Department of Molecular and Cell Biology (MCB) is one of the largest academic departments at UC Berkeley. In MCB, the study of biological processes focuses on the organization and function of organisms at the molecular and cellular level. MCB research and teaching are focused on the molecular and cellular basis of life, including biochemistry, biophysics, structural biology, cell biology, developmental biology, genetics, genomics, and neurobiology. The MCB Graduate Program is designed to prepare students for a career in research and teaching in molecular and cell biology. The program is organized into five divisions: Biochemistry, Biophysics and Structural Biology (BBS); Cell Biology, Development and Physiology (CDP); Genetics, Genomics, Evolution, and Development (GGED); Immunology and Molecular Medicine (IMM); and Neurobiology (NEU).
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Molecular and Cell Biology

Concentration name: Composition, Ethnomusicology, and Musicology
description: The Department of Music offers programs of study leading to the MA and PhD degrees in composition, ethnomusicology, and musicology. For each of these three areas of specialization, the MA is usually a prerequisite for the PhD; however, students who already hold an MA or its equivalent from another institution may be admitted directly to the PhD program. The MA/PhD program is intended for students who intend to work toward the PhD. The department does not offer a terminal MA.
Program name: Master of Arts in Music
