Concentration name: Composition, Ethnomusicology, Musicology
description: The Department of Music offers programs of study leading to the PhD degree in composition and the PhD degree in scholarship (history and literature of music or ethnomusicology). These programs are intended for students who intend to pursue careers in research and teaching at the college or university level, or in composition.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Music

Concentration name: Ancient Near Eastern Civilizations; Egyptology; Hebrew Bible/Old Testament; Islamic Studies; Jewish Studies; and Near Eastern Art and Archaeology
description: The Department of Near Eastern Studies offers graduate programs in the languages, literatures, and civilizations of the Near East from ancient times to the present. The department offers a variety of programs leading to the Master of Arts and the Doctor of Philosophy. Students choose to specialize in one of several areas: Ancient Near Eastern Civilizations; Egyptology; Hebrew Bible/Old Testament; Islamic Studies; Jewish Studies; and Near Eastern Art and Archaeology.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Near Eastern Studies

description: The Helen Wills Neuroscience Institute (HWNI) is the locus for campus-wide multidisciplinary neuroscience research at UC Berkeley. The institute is composed of over 70 faculty members from many departments including Molecular and Cell Biology, Psychology, Integrative Biology, Vision Science, Physics, Chemistry, Engineering, and Environmental Science Policy and Management. The Neuroscience Graduate Program offers a premier research and training environment for students who wish to pursue a PhD in Neuroscience. The research of the HWNI faculty spans the full breadth of modern neuroscience, from the molecules that allow neurons to communicate, to the circuits that allow us to see and hear, and the complex brain processes that underlie our behaviors, such as memory and decision making.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Neuroscience

Concentration name: Advanced Nuclear Reactors; Nuclear Materials and Manufacturing; Nuclear Waste Management; Medical Physics and Radiation Imaging
description: The Master of Engineering (MEng) program is designed for students who want to become leaders in industry and want to focus on their career in an area of technical specialization. Students will take a combination of technical courses and leadership courses, and will complete a capstone project.
Program name: Master of Engineering in Nuclear Engineering

description: The graduate programs in nuclear engineering are designed to provide a broad education in the fundamental science and technology of nuclear processes and their applications. The department offers several options for graduate study: the Master of Science (MS), the Master of Engineering (MEng), the Doctor of Philosophy (PhD), and the Doctor of Engineering (DE). Students may choose to focus their studies in areas such as nuclear reactor theory and design, nuclear materials, fusion engineering, nuclear thermal hydraulics, nuclear waste management, and nuclear non-proliferation. The MS program is designed to provide a solid foundation for more advanced study or for a career in industry or research.
Program name: Master of Science in Nuclear Engineering

description: The Department of Nuclear Engineering offers a wide range of graduate study and research in nuclear technology. In keeping with the department’s traditions, research and teaching are maintained at the highest level of scholarship. The primary areas of study and research are: applied nuclear physics; nuclear materials and chemistry; nuclear energy systems and safety analysis; and nuclear thermal hydraulics. Students can also participate in other interdisciplinary programs such as fusion research, nuclear security, bioengineering, and many more. The department also participates in the Graduate Group in Energy and Resources.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Nuclear Engineering

Concentration name: Metabolic Biology
description: The Department of Nutritional Sciences and Toxicology (NST) offers the Master of Science (MS) and the Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) degrees. The Metabolic Biology (MB) graduate program provides a comprehensive understanding of the biochemical, molecular, and physiological aspects of metabolism. The program is designed to prepare students for careers in academia, industry, and government by providing them with the necessary knowledge and research skills. Students in the program have the opportunity to work with world-class faculty on cutting-edge research projects. Research in the department spans a wide range of topics, including nutrient-gene interactions, metabolic regulation, cell signaling, and the role of nutrients and phytochemicals in health and disease. Students gain a deep understanding of the physiological and molecular mechanisms by which nutrients and toxicants affect human health.
Program name: Master of Science in Nutritional Sciences and Toxicology

Concentration name: Metabolic Biology, Toxicology
description: The Graduate Program in Nutritional Sciences and Toxicology (NST) provides students with the opportunity to pursue research in a variety of areas, including metabolic biology, molecular and cellular nutrition, and toxicology. The department's mission is to educate students in the biochemical and molecular basis of nutrient function and metabolism, and the mechanisms of action of toxic substances. Research in the department spans a wide range of topics, including the study of metabolic diseases such as obesity and diabetes, the role of nutrients in gene expression, and the impact of environmental toxins on human health.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Nutritional Sciences and Toxicology

description: The Herbert Wertheim School of Optometry & Vision Science at the University of California, Berkeley offers the Doctor of Optometry (OD) degree. Our four-year professional program (OD) leads to the Doctor of Optometry degree. Our curriculum is designed to provide you with the clinical and theoretical knowledge required for the practice of optometry. You will learn to diagnose, treat, and manage conditions and diseases of the eye and visual system. The program provides a rigorous, comprehensive curriculum that prepares students for a career in clinical practice, research, and academia. Our program combines classroom instruction, laboratory work, and extensive clinical experience.
Accreditation status: The Doctor of Optometry (OD) degree program at the University of California, Berkeley, Herbert Wertheim School of Optometry & Vision Science is accredited by the Accreditation Council on Optometric Education (ACOE).
Program name: Doctor of Optometry

description: The UC Berkeley PhD in Performance Studies is an interdisciplinary program that draws on a wide range of faculty and resources from across the campus. It is designed to provide students with a rigorous foundation in the history, theory, and practice of performance, with a particular focus on the ways in which performance intersects with social, political, and cultural issues. Students in the program have the opportunity to work with faculty from a variety of departments, including Theater, Dance, and Performance Studies; Music; Rhetoric; English; Anthropology; and Ethnic Studies, among others. The program prepares students for careers in academia, as well as for leadership roles in the arts and other fields.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Performance Studies

description: The graduate program in philosophy is designed to lead to the degree of Doctor of Philosophy. The program provides a strong foundation in the history of philosophy and the main areas of contemporary philosophical inquiry, while allowing students to specialize in their areas of interest. The department offers courses and seminars in logic, ethics, social and political philosophy, metaphysics, epistemology, philosophy of mind, philosophy of language, philosophy of science, and the history of philosophy (including ancient, medieval, and modern).
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Philosophy

description: The Ph.D. program is designed to give students a thorough grounding in the fundamental principles of physics and to provide them with the opportunity to do original research in a variety of experimental and theoretical areas. During their first two years, students take a core of courses to prepare them for the Preliminary Examination and for research. These courses include: graduate-level classical mechanics, quantum mechanics, statistical mechanics, and electricity and magnetism. In addition, students are encouraged to begin research as soon as possible. After passing the Preliminary Examination, students choose a research advisor and a research area.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Physics

description: The PhD program in Plant Biology at UC Berkeley provides training in modern plant biology, including genomics, proteomics, and molecular, cellular, and genetic analysis. The program’s goal is to provide students with a broad and solid foundation in the various areas of plant biology, as well as to develop their skills in independent research. Our graduate students are part of a tight-knit community that includes over 40 faculty members and approximately 100 students.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Plant Biology

Concentration name: American Politics, Comparative Politics, International Relations, Models and Politics, Political Theory, and Quantitative Methods
description: The Department of Political Science offers a program of graduate study leading to the degree of Doctor of Philosophy. The program is designed to prepare students for careers in research and teaching, and for other professional careers. It provides students with a broad knowledge of the field of political science and with the skills necessary to conduct original research.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Political Science

Concentration name: Clinical Science
description: The Clinical Science Program at the University of California, Berkeley is a member of the Academy of Psychological Clinical Science, which is an alliance of leading, scientifically oriented, doctoral and internship training programs in clinical and health psychology in the United States and Canada. Clinical Science at Berkeley is also a charter member of the PCSAS (Psychological Clinical Science Accreditation System). Our program is designed to provide students with the knowledge and skills necessary to pursue careers in research and teaching, and to provide clinical services in a variety of settings. The program is committed to a training model that integrates research and practice.
Accreditation status: The Clinical Science Program at the University of California, Berkeley is accredited by the American Psychological Association (APA) and the Psychological Clinical Science Accreditation System (PCSAS).
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Psychology

Concentration name: Biostatistics, Environmental Health Sciences, Epidemiology, Epidemiology/Biostatistics, Health and Social Behavior, Health Policy and Management, Infectious Diseases and Vaccinology, Interdisciplinary, Maternal, Child, and Adolescent Health, Public Health Nutrition
description: The Master of Public Health (MPH) is the most common professional degree for those who wish to pursue a career in public health. The program provides a strong foundation in the core disciplines of public health while allowing students to specialize in their area of interest. The UC Berkeley School of Public Health aims to improve population health, especially for the most vulnerable, through high-quality research and education. We prepare tomorrow’s health leaders, perform transformative research, and bring together the power of local and global communities. The degree is offered in several areas of study and in a variety of formats, including two-year, 11-month, 4+1, and online tracks.
Accreditation status: The UC Berkeley School of Public Health is fully accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH).
Program name: Master of Public Health

Concentration name: Biostatistics, Environmental Health Sciences, Epidemiology, Health Policy and Management
description: The School of Public Health offers several programs of study leading to the following degrees: Master of Public Health (MPH), Master of Arts (MA), Master of Science (MS), Doctor of Public Health (DrPH), and Doctor of Philosophy (PhD). The Master of Public Health degree is a professional degree, designed to prepare students for a career in public health practice. The MA, MS, and PhD degrees are academic degrees, designed for students interested in a career in research or teaching. The DrPH degree is a professional degree, designed for students interested in a career in public health leadership and practice.
Accreditation status: The UC Berkeley School of Public Health is fully accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH).
Program name: Master of Science in Public Health

Concentration name: Environmental Health Sciences, Epidemiology, Health Policy, and Infectious Diseases and Immunity
description: The Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Public Health is a research-oriented degree that provides students with the advanced knowledge and skills necessary to conduct independent research and to teach in public health and related fields. The program emphasizes the application of rigorous research methods to address complex public health problems. The program offers several areas of concentration, including Environmental Health Sciences, Epidemiology, Health Policy, and Infectious Diseases and Immunity.
Accreditation status: The UC Berkeley School of Public Health is fully accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH).
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Public Health

description: The UC Berkeley Doctor of Public Health (DrPH) is a school-wide interdisciplinary program that prepares graduates for high-level careers in public health leadership. The DrPH degree is the highest professional degree in the field of public health. This program provides students with the leadership, management, and advocacy skills to solve complex public health problems. Our students are diverse in their backgrounds and interests, and they are committed to making a difference in the world. The DrPH program is a small, highly selective, school-wide program. Students customize their curriculum based on their professional experience, professional interests, and career goals.
Accreditation status: The UC Berkeley School of Public Health is accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH).
Program name: Doctor of Public Health

description: The Goldman School’s Master of Public Policy (MPP) program is a two-year, full-time program that emphasizes the application of analytical tools to a wide range of policy issues. The curriculum includes courses in microeconomics, quantitative analysis, political and organizational analysis, and legal analysis. Students also complete a policy internship and a Master’s thesis (Policy Analysis Exercise).
Program name: Master of Public Policy

description: The doctoral program is designed to prepare students for careers in university teaching and advanced policy research. It is a small, research-oriented program, with about two or three graduates per year. The program allows students to develop highly focused expertise in a particular policy area, while also becoming versatile in the multiple methodologies of public policy analysis. Our students work closely with the Goldman School faculty and are encouraged to collaborate with other faculty and doctoral students across the UC Berkeley campus.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Public Policy

description: The Range Management Graduate Group offers a program of study leading to an MS degree in Range Management. This program is coordinated by the Department of Environmental Science, Policy, and Management. Range management is the specialized system of land management used to provide consumer goods and ecosystem services from non-arable lands. These lands, which include grasslands, shrublands, woodlands, and deserts, are managed by ecological rather than agronomic methods. The master’s program is designed to provide students with a) a solid foundation in the concepts and methods of range management and b) an opportunity to explore a specific problem in range management. It is particularly suited to students who have a bachelor’s degree in range management, forestry, or a related field and who wish to pursue a career in the management of rangeland resources.
Program name: Master of Science in Range Management

description: The Master of Real Estate Development + Design (MRED+D) at UC Berkeley’s College of Environmental Design is an intensive, 11-month professional graduate degree program. Our curriculum centers on the four pillars of real estate development: finance, design, law, and construction. It also uniquely incorporates the principles of equity, sustainability, and resilience, preparing you to lead the creation of sustainable and vibrant urban environments. The program is designed to bridge the gap between design and real estate development, equipping students with the skills to address the complex challenges of urban development in the 21st century.
Program name: Master of Real Estate Development + Design

description: The Rhetoric Department is a leading center for interdisciplinary research in the humanities and social sciences. The program's strength is its multifaceted approach to the study of the history and theory of rhetorical discourse in its various forms: political, legal, scientific, and aesthetic. Rhetoric is also a primary site for the study of contemporary theory and for the development of new approaches to the study of images and visual culture. The department's faculty is known for its wide-ranging intellectual reach, and its graduate students often pursue research that crosses traditional disciplinary boundaries.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Rhetoric

description: The interdisciplinary PhD program in Romance Languages and Literatures (RLL) is offered by the departments of French, Italian Studies, and Spanish & Portuguese. Candidates work toward the PhD in Romance Languages and Literatures with an emphasis on a combination of two of the three Romance languages/literatures: French, Italian, and Spanish/Portuguese. The RLL program is designed for students whose interest in these languages and literatures and their corresponding cultures and linguistics requires a broader angle of vision than is found in a single-language department. Students specialize in two of the languages/literatures taught in the three departments (French, Italian, Spanish & Portuguese). One is designated as the student's major language, the other as the minor language. Students take courses in both languages and literatures, and they may be asked to teach in both. RLL students are also encouraged to make use of Berkeley’s many other departments and programs (e.g., Comparative Literature, Film Studies, Linguistics, Women’s Studies) to further their research and help form their dissertation committees.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Romance Languages and Literatures

description: The Department of Scandinavian offers a program of study leading to the MA and PhD in Scandinavian languages and literatures. The program is designed to provide students with a broad knowledge of Scandinavian literature, culture, and linguistics, and a high level of proficiency in at least one Scandinavian language. Students specialize in either the medieval or the modern period.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Scandinavian Languages and Literatures

Concentration name: Russian Literature, Czech Literature, Polish Literature, South Slavic Literature, or Slavic Linguistics
description: The Department of Slavic Languages and Literatures offers programs of study leading to the MA and PhD degrees. Students are required to choose a major field (Russian, Czech, Polish, or South Slavic literatures or Slavic linguistics). To ensure that students receive a broad background, they must also choose two minor fields, one of which must be in a Slavic field (unless the major is Slavic linguistics, in which case both minors may be outside the field). This requirement may be satisfied by a minor in another Slavic literature or in Slavic linguistics, or by a minor in a related field such as another literature, history, or linguistics. All PhD students are required to take a pedagogy course in their second year and must complete at least two semesters of apprentice teaching. UC Berkeley Slavic graduates are distinguished by their preparation as both scholars and teachers. Members of the faculty represent a wide range of interests and approaches to the study of literature and linguistics.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Slavic Languages and Literatures

description: The School of Social Welfare and the School of Public Health offer a concurrent degree program for students who wish to pursue a career in the field of public health social work. This program is designed to provide students with the necessary knowledge and skills for effective practice at the intersection of these two fields. It offers a comprehensive and integrated approach to social welfare and public health, with a focus on addressing the social determinants of health and promoting health equity. The concurrent degree program is a three-year program. It is designed to be completed in six semesters of full-time study. At the end of three years, the student will have earned both the Master of Social Welfare (MSW) and the Master of Public Health (MPH) degrees.
Accreditation status: The MSW program at UC Berkeley is fully accredited by the Council on Social Work Education (CSWE). The UC Berkeley School of Public Health is accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH).
Program name: Master of Social Welfare

description: Berkeley Social Welfare’s PhD program prepares students for careers as scholars, researchers, and educators in the field of social welfare. Our program offers a rigorous, interdisciplinary curriculum designed to foster deep knowledge of social problems and the policies and practices designed to address them. Our PhD students learn to conduct independent research that contributes to the scientific knowledge base of the profession and informs social welfare policy and practice.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Social Welfare

description: The graduate program in sociology at Berkeley is designed for students who are interested in pursuing a Ph.D. It is primarily intended to prepare students for research and teaching in sociology, although some of our graduates also work in other fields. The department is a community of scholars including 30 faculty members and approximately 100 graduate students.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Sociology

Concentration name: South Asian Studies, Southeast Asian Studies
description: The Department of South & Southeast Asian Studies offers graduate programs leading to the Master of Arts (MA) and Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) degrees in South and Southeast Asian Studies. The MA and PhD programs are intended for students who wish to pursue a career in research and teaching at the university level or to apply their knowledge of South or Southeast Asian languages and cultures in other professional contexts. Within the PhD program, there are two distinct tracks: South Asian Studies and Southeast Asian Studies. The South Asian Studies track is designed to provide students with a deep and wide-ranging knowledge of the languages and cultures of the South Asian subcontinent. Students choose a primary language of concentration (Sanskrit, Hindi, Urdu, Tamil, etc.) and a field of specialization (Literature, Religion, Philosophy, History, or Social Sciences). The Southeast Asian Studies track is designed to provide students with a deep and wide-ranging knowledge of the languages and cultures of the Southeast Asian region. Students choose a primary language of concentration (Indonesian, Khmer, Tagalog, Thai, Vietnamese, etc.) and a field of specialization (Literature, Religion, Philosophy, History, or Social Sciences).
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in South and Southeast Asian Studies

Concentration name: Iberian and Latin American Literatures and Cultures; Luso-Brazilian Literatures and Cultures; Romance Languages and Literatures; Hispanic Languages and Literatures
description: The graduate program in Spanish and Portuguese at Berkeley provides students with the most comprehensive education in the literatures, cultures, and languages of the Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking worlds. The department offers the MA/PhD and PhD degrees in Spanish and Portuguese, with concentrations in Iberian and Latin American Literatures and Cultures and Luso-Brazilian Literatures and Cultures. We also participate in two interdisciplinary doctoral programs: Romance Languages and Literatures (offered in conjunction with the Departments of French and Italian) and Hispanic Languages and Literatures (offered in conjunction with the Department of Linguistics).
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Spanish and Portuguese

description: The Department of Statistics offers three degree programs: the Ph.D., the M.A., and the Professional Master of Financial Engineering (MFE). Students in the Ph.D. program and M.A. program receive a solid foundation in statistical theory and practice. Faculty members are involved in a wide range of research projects in theoretical and applied statistics. Graduate students and faculty members benefit from the department's close ties with many researchers across the Berkeley campus and at the nearby Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory. These groups offer a regular flow of visitors, many of whom give talks in the several departmental seminars. M.A. Degree: The M.A. in Statistics provides a solid foundation in statistical theory and practice and can be used as a springboard for a statistics or data science career in a variety of industries. This is a small, selective, and very fast-paced program that is usually completed in two semesters (one academic year).
Program name: Master of Arts in Statistics

description: The doctoral program in statistics is designed to give students a comprehensive knowledge of the theory and methods of statistics and probability. It is intended for students with a strong mathematical background and an interest in any area of statistics or probability. Research interests of faculty and students include many areas of statistical theory and methodology, probability theory, and the application of statistics and probability to many fields, including the biological and physical sciences, social sciences, and engineering.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Statistics

description: The Master of Translational Medicine (MTM) program is a joint effort between the Department of Bioengineering at UC Berkeley and the Department of Bioengineering and Therapeutic Sciences at UCSF. The program is designed to provide students with the tools and network to take a medical innovation from the lab to the clinic. The curriculum combines engineering, clinical, and business training to prepare students for careers in the biotech and medical device industries, teaching essential skills to move innovations through the pipeline from the lab to the bedside.
Program name: Master of Translational Medicine

description: The Master of Urban Design (MUD) is a one-year (three semester) post-professional degree for those who already have a professional degree in architecture, landscape architecture, or city and regional planning. The program aims to train future leaders of urban design who can address the complex challenges of making and managing the urban environment in a rapidly urbanizing world. Urban design is an interdisciplinary field, and the program at Berkeley brings together faculty and students from the departments of Architecture, City & Regional Planning, and Landscape Architecture & Environmental Planning. The MUD program is centered on the urban design studio. Projects are based on real-world sites in the San Francisco Bay Area and elsewhere, and explore a wide range of urban scales, from the street and the block to the neighborhood and the region.
Program name: Master of Urban Design

description: The Vision Science Graduate Program provides comprehensive training in the many aspects of vision science, from the molecular biology of the eye to the psychology and neurophysiology of perception. The program is designed to prepare students for careers in research and teaching. The Vision Science Program at UC Berkeley is an interdisciplinary program where students study the biology, physics, and psychology of sight and its impact on individuals and society. The program offers students a broad foundation in vision science while allowing them to specialize in a specific area of research, with access to state-of-the-art research facilities and world-renowned faculty.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Vision Science

description: The Designated Emphasis in Critical Theory (DE) provides graduate students already enrolled in a PhD program at UC Berkeley with a curricular and research framework for studying the history and current developments of critical theory. The program is intended to offer students a systematic approach to the diverse traditions of critical thought that have informed modern scholarship across the humanities and social sciences. Students who complete the requirements of the DE receive a certificate of completion and the designation 'Critical Theory' on their official transcript and diploma.
Program name: Designated Emphasis in Critical Theory

description: The Designated Emphasis in Folklore (DE) is a program for graduate students at UC Berkeley who are interested in the study of folklore and traditional culture. It is intended to provide a systematic and integrated curriculum of study for students who wish to pursue a concentration in folklore as part of their PhD program. The Designated Emphasis in Folklore is not a degree-granting program. Rather, it is an interdisciplinary program that offers a specialization in folklore to students who are already enrolled in a PhD program at UC Berkeley.
Program name: Designated Emphasis in Folklore

description: The Designated Emphasis (DE) in Women, Gender, and Sexuality provides graduate students with the opportunity to specialize in women, gender, and sexuality studies while completing their PhD degree. It is designed to provide a formal structure for interdisciplinary work and to recognize the importance of research and teaching in this area. The DE offers students a program of study that includes a core course, electives, and a dissertation with a significant focus on women, gender, and/or sexuality.
Program name: Designated Emphasis in Women, Gender, and Sexuality

description: The Designated Emphasis (DE) in European Studies is available to Berkeley Ph.D. students in any department or program. It provides an opportunity for students to engage in interdisciplinary research on Europe, and to have that expertise recognized with a formal credential. Students must satisfy requirements in three categories: course work, a required language, and a dissertation with a European focus. Students should apply as soon as they decide to pursue the DE. The latest a student can apply is one semester before the Ph.D. qualifying exam.
Program name: Designated Emphasis in European Studies

description: The Nanoscale Science and Engineering Graduate Group (NSEGG) offers a Designated Emphasis (DE) in Nanoscale Science and Engineering (NSE). The DE in NSE is an interdisciplinary program that provides graduate students with a comprehensive education in the fundamental science and engineering of nanoscale structures. NSE is a rapidly growing field with profound implications for technology, medicine, and the environment. The program aims to train the next generation of researchers and leaders in this exciting field, fostering cross-disciplinary collaboration and providing students with the skills and knowledge needed to excel in this competitive landscape.
Program name: Designated Emphasis in Nanoscale Science and Engineering

description: The Designated Emphasis in Energy Science and Technology (DEEST) is an interdisciplinary program that provides a framework for doctoral students to specialize in energy science and technology. The program is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in the fundamental principles of energy science and technology, and to introduce them to the social, economic, and policy aspects of energy systems. The DEEST provides an opportunity for doctoral students from a variety of engineering and science departments to engage in a curriculum that includes energy-related coursework and research.
Program name: Designated Emphasis in Energy Sciences and Technology

description: The Designated Emphasis in Communication, Computation and Statistics (DECCS) provides students with a strong background in the methods of communication, computation, and statistics, as applied to the social sciences. The DECCS is intended for doctoral students in social science departments (e.g., Sociology, Political Science, Economics, etc.) who want to learn how to apply these methods to their research. The DECCS provides a curriculum that covers the fundamentals of communication, computation, and statistics, as well as more advanced topics in these areas. Students who complete the DECCS will be well-prepared for careers in academia, government, and the private sector. Upon successful completion of the dissertation and the DECCS requirements, the student’s transcript will include the notation ‘Designated Emphasis in Communication, Computation and Statistics’.
Program name: Designated Emphasis in Communication, Computation and Statistics

description: Computational biology is a central field in modern biology. The Designated Emphasis in Computational and Genomic Biology (DE CGB) is intended to provide curriculum and training in the field to students in doctoral programs across the Berkeley campus. The DE CGB provides students with a solid foundation in the principles of biology, statistics, and computer science, as well as the ability to apply these principles to the analysis of genomic data.
Program name: Designated Emphasis in Computational and Genomic Biology

description: The Designated Emphasis (DE) in New Media provides Berkeley doctoral students with a set of curricular and research resources for studying the impact of new media on traditional disciplines. It is an interdisciplinary program that involves more than two dozen faculty from across the campus. The DE provides students with a common set of theoretical and methodological tools for research on new media and brings them into a community of researchers who are exploring the field.
Program name: Designated Emphasis in New Media

description: The Graduate Designated Emphasis (DE) in Global Urban Humanities provides an interdisciplinary framework for the study of the city. Students investigate the histories and cultures of cities as they interact with the physical and social environments. The curriculum includes a core course, Global Urban Humanities: Theories and Methods, and two electives, as well as an interdisciplinary research studio. The DE allows students in the humanities, social sciences, and environmental design to engage in shared study and research, bridging the gap between descriptive and interpretive methods and the projective and diagnostic tools of the design and planning disciplines. Students in PhD programs across the campus are eligible to apply.
Program name: Designated Emphasis in Global Urban Humanities

description: Development Engineering (DE) is an interdisciplinary field that addresses the problems of people living in poverty. Building on the core strengths of UC Berkeley in engineering and the social sciences, the program focuses on creating technology-based solutions to solve global development problems. The DE provides students with a set of tools to create, pilot, and evaluate technology that could improve the lives of those in low-resource settings. Students learn how to measure the impact of their work and how to think about the economic and social context of their technical solutions.
Program name: Designated Emphasis in Development Engineering

description: The Designated Emphasis (DE) in Science and Technology Studies (STS) provides a curated course of study for Berkeley PhD students who want to develop a rigorous, interdisciplinary approach to their work. The program is designed to provide students with a theoretical and methodological foundation in the social studies of science, technology and medicine. It is intended to help students from a wide range of disciplines to communicate with researchers from other fields, and to facilitate the development of a common set of questions and research methods. The DE will provide students with a formal credential in STS, and will help to create a community of scholars who are interested in the social and cultural dimensions of science and technology. Students who complete the DE will be better prepared to participate in the global conversation about the role of science and technology in society, and will be better positioned for academic and professional opportunities in this growing field.
Program name: Designated Emphasis in Science and Technology Studies

description: The Designated Emphasis (DE) in Dutch Studies is a program that provides a framework for regular and structured contact among graduate students and faculty in different disciplines who study Dutch history, culture, linguistics, and literature. The Dutch Studies program is unique in its breadth and its interdisciplinary nature. Its goals are: To provide a structure for graduate students who would like to study Dutch history, culture, linguistics, or literature in a more formal way. To foster an interdisciplinary approach to Dutch Studies and to create a community of scholars who work in these areas. For students who choose this DE, the PhD degree will be designated with the name of the home department and the program, for example: “PhD in History with a Designated Emphasis in Dutch Studies.”
Program name: Designated Emphasis in Dutch Studies

description: The Designated Emphasis in Indigenous Language Revitalization (DEILR) is an interdisciplinary program that offers graduate students from any department at UC Berkeley the opportunity to gain expertise in the theory and practice of language revitalization. The program is designed to prepare students for academic and professional work in this field by providing them with a solid foundation in the linguistic, pedagogical, and social aspects of language revitalization.
Program name: Designated Emphasis in Indigenous Language Revitalization

description: The Designated Emphasis (DE) in Renaissance and Early Modern Studies (REMS) provides a framework for regular exchange among faculty and graduate students in different departments at Berkeley and a way to coordinate and foster the interdisciplinary study of the early modern period (roughly 1350–1750). The Designated Emphasis is open to graduate students already enrolled in a Ph.D. program in any department or school at UC Berkeley. Since 2001, students from Architecture, Comparative Literature, English, French, German, History, History of Art, Italian Studies, Music, Near Eastern Studies, Philosophy, Rhetoric, South and Southeast Asian Studies, and Spanish and Portuguese have been part of the program.
Program name: Designated Emphasis in Renaissance and Early Modern Studies

description: The Designated Emphasis (DE) in Southeast Asian Studies (SEAS) provides a framework for regularized interdisciplinary collaboration and for the professional certification of graduate students who are currently enrolled in a PhD program at UC Berkeley and whose work has a significant focus on Southeast Asia. There is a growing number of doctoral students at Berkeley in various departments and disciplines who work on some aspect of Southeast Asia. Often these students have few opportunities to interact with each other, and they frequently feel somewhat isolated within their own departments. The Designated Emphasis in Southeast Asian Studies aims to create a community of Southeast Asianists on the Berkeley campus. Its main goal is to promote a multi-disciplinary approach to Southeast Asian studies by providing students with a systematic way of identifying a core of faculty and other students with whom they can work as they proceed through their training.
Program name: Designated Emphasis in Southeast Asian Studies

description: The Graduate Certificate in Applied Data Science is a program for UC Berkeley graduate students in any department. The certificate program allows students to gain the skills they need to navigate the world of data and big data. Students learn the latest techniques for collecting, cleaning, analyzing, and visualizing data, and gain experience with a wide range of data science tools and technologies.
Program name: Graduate Certificate in Applied Data Science

description: The Graduate Certificate in Food Systems is an interdisciplinary program that allows graduate students to gain a broad and comprehensive understanding of the complex factors that influence food systems. This certificate program is open to all graduate students at UC Berkeley and is designed to provide students with the necessary tools to address the multifaceted challenges of creating a more sustainable, equitable, and healthy food system. The certificate provides a framework for students to explore how different aspects of food systems—from production and processing to distribution and consumption—are interconnected and influence health, environment, and society. Students will develop the skills to analyze and address these complexities through interdisciplinary coursework and a capstone project.
Program name: Graduate Certificate in Food Systems

description: The Graduate Certificate in Global Urban Humanities is a certificate program for UC Berkeley graduate students in any department who are interested in the study of cities and urban life through a combination of humanistic and design/social science methods. The program is part of the Global Urban Humanities Initiative, a joint project of the Arts & Humanities Division and the College of Environmental Design. The certificate provides a framework for students to engage in interdisciplinary research and pedagogy, offering a curriculum that includes an introductory core colloquium, elective courses from departments outside the student's home discipline, and a research-intensive capstone requirement such as an interdisciplinary studio or research seminar.
Program name: Graduate Certificate in Global Urban Humanities

description: The Graduate Certificate in Real Estate (GCRE) is available to any student currently enrolled in a graduate degree program at UC Berkeley. The certificate is a way to gain further knowledge in real estate that may not be available in their home department, and to give students a competitive edge in the job market. It is an interdisciplinary program that includes the Haas School of Business, the College of Environmental Design, the Berkeley Law School, and the Goldman School of Public Policy. The certificate is administered by the Fisher Center for Real Estate and Urban Economics at the Haas School of Business.
Program name: Graduate Certificate in Real Estate

description: The Certificate in Teaching and Learning in Higher Education provides a structure for GSIs to refine their teaching skills and to provide them with a credential for the academic job market. The program is sponsored by the GSI Teaching & Resource Center and the Graduate Council of the Academic Senate. To receive the certificate, participants must complete a sequence of activities: a pedagogy course, teaching experience, teaching observations, and a teaching portfolio. The certificate program aims to: (1) assist GSIs in enhancing their teaching while at UC Berkeley, (2) prepare GSIs for the teaching responsibilities they will assume as future faculty, (3) provide GSIs with a credential for the job market, and (4) identify GSIs on campus who have a significant commitment to teaching and learning.
Program name: Graduate Certificate in Teaching and Learning in Higher Education
